keys.description: THE deployment input: the stack's gateway. Every meeting verb reaches it with the caller's own key, and the other service URLs default around it — a deployment that names one URL works.
The gateway, when it is not where VEXA_URL points. Split deployments only.
agent-api — the workspace, claim-book, settings, queue, friction and terms routes every workspace verb forwards to.
admin-api — accounts, and the per-user gateway key this edge mints once and remembers.
flows-api — the fact intake, the reaction projection and the timeline. Unset on a deployment without the flows engine; those verbs then say so by name and nothing else changes.

The name this edge PUBLISHES. It drives the sign-in links, the agent bootstrap and the transport's DNS-rebinding host guard — a server that publishes one name while admitting another refuses its own users.

keys.default: (empty — deeplink then answers with no origin rather than a well-formed dead link)
keys.description: The minutes terminal every deeplink opens. The SAME name flows reads, deliberately: two spellings of the host is how a link that names a host the person cannot reach gets minted.

admin-api's operator token. The rig read this by running `docker inspect vexa-dogfood-admin-api-1` and splitting that container's environment — a docker socket and a hardcoded container name, for a string (seam inventory B6.2). It is a credential and it arrives like one.
flows-api's operator key. Unset ⇒ the flows verbs are not configured here; they say so by name and every other tool is unaffected.

The HMAC key agent-api mints per-dispatch `vxd_` tokens with. UNSET REFUSES EVERY DELEGATION: a zero-length HMAC key verifies for anyone who knows the format, so 'not configured here' must mean nobody gets in.
The stack's internal secret (#526), same name and same value as the rest of the internal tier. A server-to-server caller presents it where a person would present a token.

The regime for a workspace nothing has been recorded about. `cloud` = the files live on the stack. `local` = the files live on the person's machine and no cloud agent runs for them; the workspace verbs still operate on the cloud copy and git is the sync.

OFF in the product, and off BY DEFAULT here — the rig defaulted it on. It enables the `token=` call-argument fallback and the `GET /do` bridge, both of which put a credential in a query string: right for a fetch-only agent on a private host, wrong anywhere requests are logged.
The dev lane's inbox. Unset in a real deployment, which is what makes `mail_inbox`/`mail_read` answer 'not configured here' rather than inventing one.
Where the sign-in code is posted. The code goes over the same channel the product lives on, so a person proving they read that mailbox is the whole authentication.
Port for the same.
The mailbox a rehearsal drives when it needs one. Operator verbs only.
Where `vexa_overview` and `vexa_search_docs` read from — the two tools that answer before anybody has an account.

The ONLY directory this service writes: durable tokens, pending sign-in codes, the per-person gateway keys it minted, converted transcript fixtures. A volume in a deployment. `tests/test_thin_forward.py` asserts no tool writes anywhere else.

keys.default: (empty — loopback plus the host in VEXA_PUBLIC_MCP_URL)
keys.description: Extra Host headers the transport will answer to, comma separated. The SDK's DNS-rebinding guard defaults to localhost-only for a loopback bind, so a deployment behind more than one name says so here rather than turning the guard off.
The port this service listens on.

platform_admin.description: Reaching admin-api as the platform operator: resolving an account by email, creating one during sign-in, and minting the per-person gateway key every meeting verb travels on.
platform_admin.when_unconfigured: Sign-in and every gateway-backed verb answer with the service's own refusal (admin-api 401), named, rather than a tool pretending the account does not exist.

flows.description: The flows engine: facts in, reactions out, the timeline, and the scheduled-join projection.
flows.when_unconfigured: The flows verbs return `unavailable: <tool>` naming this key; every other tool on the server is unaffected.

delegation.description: Accepting the short-lived, scoped `vxd_` token agent-api mints per dispatch, instead of a durable user credential in a spawned container.
delegation.when_unconfigured: Every delegation token is refused — deliberately, and closed: an empty HMAC key would verify for anyone who knows the format.

internal_tier.description: Server-to-server callers presenting the stack's internal secret where a person would present a token.
internal_tier.when_unconfigured: Only person-shaped credentials authenticate; an internal caller is anonymous.

mail_double.description: Reading what the product actually sent, as a person receives it — the dev lane's inbox.
mail_double.when_unconfigured: `mail_inbox` and `mail_read` say the inbox is not configured here.
